category: Output Jobs, manufacturing data, documentation & export
description: Turning an Altium project into deliverables: the Output Job editor and its output containers, fabrication outputs (Gerber, Gerber X2, ODB++, IPC-2581, NC drill, test point and stack reports), assembly outputs (pick and place, assembly drawings, Draftsman), report outputs (BOM, netlist, cross reference), documentation outputs (PDF, prints, 3D PDF), validation outputs, and the interchange exporters to MCAD, simulation and analysis tools.

tools.name: Output Job file (OutJob)
tools.description: A reusable, named configuration of every output a project needs, stored as an .OutJob document inside the project. Outputs are listed by category (Netlist, Simulator, Documentation, Assembly, Fabrication, Report, Validation, Export, Post Processing) and each is wired to an output container that decides where and in what form the result is written. Running the OutJob regenerates the whole deliverable set in one click and is what the Project Releaser executes.
tools.usage: File > New > Output Job File; add outputs with 'Add New … Output'; wire each to a container; click Generate content / Run

parameters.name: Output container
parameters.description: Folder Structure, PDF, Video or Print — one container can receive many outputs.

parameters.name: Data source
parameters.description: Which document or the whole project each output is generated from.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: Which assembly variant the output represents.

parameters.name: Enabled / Generate content
parameters.description: Per-output enable and the button that produces the files.

tools.example: New OutJob > add Gerber X2, NC Drill, IPC-2581, BOM and Draftsman outputs > wire the first four to a 'Folder Structure' container and the drawings to a 'PDF' container > Generate content.
tools.notes: Keep separate OutJobs for Fabrication, Assembly and Documentation so a release publishes a coherent, reviewable set rather than one giant folder.

tools.name: Output containers
tools.description: Where an OutJob's results go. Folder Structure writes files to a path built from tokens such as [Project Name] and [Output Type]; PDF merges the selected outputs into one bookmarked document with optional net and component hyperlinks; Print sends them to a printer; Video renders a 3D fly-through. Containers also control whether the output opens after generation and whether it is added to the project.
tools.usage: OutJob editor > Output Containers column > Add New Output Container > Folder Structure / PDF / Print / Video
tools.example: Create a Folder Structure container with the path `[Release Vault Folder]\Fabrication` and 'Use relative path' ticked, then wire the Gerber and NC Drill outputs into it.

tools.name: Gerber files output
tools.description: Classic RS-274X photoplot output. The setup chooses units and format (2:3, 2:4, 2:5 in inches or the metric equivalents), which layers are plotted, the drill-drawing and drill-guide symbol layers, whether mechanical layers are added to every plot, and advanced options such as G54 aperture selection and film-box size. Still the most widely accepted format.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > Gerber Files…; or add a Gerber Files output in an OutJob

parameters.name: Units / Format
parameters.description: Inches or millimetres and the coordinate resolution; 2:4 inches or 4:4 mm is typical.

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Which copper, mask, paste, overlay, keep-out, drill and mechanical layers are plotted.

parameters.name: Drill Drawing / Drill Guide
parameters.description: Which layer pairs get a drill drawing and symbol legend.

parameters.name: Include unconnected mid-layer pads
parameters.description: Whether unconnected inner pads are plotted.

tools.example: Fabrication Outputs > Gerber Files > Units mm, Format 4:4 > Layers: plot all used layers, Mechanical 1 added to all > Advanced: tick 'Generate DRC Rules export file'.
tools.notes: Always open the generated Gerbers in the CAM Editor (File > Open the .apr/.gbr set) and compare against the board before releasing.

tools.name: Gerber X2 output
tools.description: The extended Gerber format that embeds attributes describing each file's function (copper layer and its index, soldermask, paste, profile), the netlist, pad functions and component data. A fabricator reading X2 needs no layer-mapping spreadsheet, which removes the single most common source of fabrication errors.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > Gerber X2 Files…; or add a Gerber X2 output in an OutJob
tools.example: Fabrication Outputs > Gerber X2 > Units mm, Format 4:4, tick the netlist attributes > Generate; the output carries the stackup and net data inside the files.
tools.notes: Confirm the fabricator accepts X2; a few older CAM systems still expect plain RS-274X plus a layer list.

tools.name: ODB++ output
tools.description: Writes the Valor ODB++ intelligent data set: copper, masks, paste, drills, stackup, netlist, component placement and attributes in a single directory tree or archive. Because it is one self-describing package, it eliminates layer mapping and netlist mismatch entirely and is preferred by most assembly houses.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > ODB++ Files…; or add an ODB++ output in an OutJob
tools.example: Fabrication Outputs > ODB++ Files > tick 'Export ODB++ as a compressed file' and include the netlist > Generate.

tools.name: IPC-2581 output
tools.description: The open intelligent-data standard: an XML package carrying the stackup, copper, drills, netlist, components, BOM and DFM data. Like ODB++ it is a single, unambiguous handoff, and being a published standard it is not tied to one CAM vendor. Revision B or C is selected in the output setup.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > IPC-2581 Files…; or add an IPC-2581 output in an OutJob
tools.example: Fabrication Outputs > IPC-2581 > Revision C > include BOM and netlist > Generate; the fabricator loads one file.

tools.name: NC Drill output
tools.description: Excellon drill files plus the tool table. Options set units and format, leading/trailing zero handling, whether plated and non-plated holes go to separate files, whether to generate separate files per drill pair (needed for blind and buried vias), whether slots are written as routed paths, and whether to optimise the change count.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > NC Drill Files…; or add an NC Drill output in an OutJob

parameters.name: Units / Format
parameters.description: Must match what the fabricator expects; mismatched zero suppression is a classic scrap cause.

parameters.name: Generate separate NC Drill files for plated & non-plated holes
parameters.description: Standard practice, and required for correct PTH/NPTH processing.

parameters.name: Generate board edge rout paths
parameters.description: Writes the profile as a routing path for the CNC.

tools.example: Fabrication Outputs > NC Drill Files > Units mm, Format 4:4, separate plated/non-plated, optimise change location > Generate.

tools.name: Drill Drawing / Drill Table
tools.description: The documentation counterpart to the drill file: a plot showing each hole with its assigned symbol plus a legend table of symbol, size, plating, tolerance and count. It is generated as part of the Gerber set (Drill Drawing/Guide layers) or, more legibly, placed as a live Drill Table in a Draftsman document.
tools.usage: Included in the Gerber Files output's Drill Drawing tab; or Draftsman: Place > Drill Table
tools.example: In Draftsman: Place > Board Fabrication View, then Place > Drill Table — the table updates automatically when a via size changes.

tools.name: Test Point Report
tools.description: Lists every assigned fabrication or assembly test point with its net, coordinates, side and pad type, in the format expected by the test-fixture house. It is generated from the test points assigned by the Testpoint Manager under the test point rules.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > Test Point Report…; or add it as a Fabrication output in an OutJob
tools.example: Assign test points with Tools > Testpoint Manager, then Fabrication Outputs > Test Point Report > IPC-D-356A and text formats > Generate.

tools.name: IPC-D-356A netlist export
tools.description: The standard netlist format for bare-board electrical test: it gives the fabricator the intended connectivity with pad coordinates so the flying-probe or bed-of-nails test verifies the board against the design rather than against itself. Sending it with the Gerbers is what makes 'electrically tested' meaningful.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > Test Point Report (IPC-D-356A) / Design > Netlist > IPC-D-356A; or as an output in an OutJob
tools.example: Add an IPC-D-356A netlist output to the fabrication OutJob so every release ships with a test netlist.

tools.name: Board Stack Report / Layer Stackup Legend
tools.description: Documents the construction: a report of every layer with material, thickness, copper weight and dielectric properties, and the impedance profiles with their calculated geometries. In Draftsman the same data is placed as a live Layer Stack Legend that updates with the stackup.
tools.usage: Reports > Board Stack Report; Draftsman: Place > Layer Stack Legend; also available as a Fabrication output
tools.example: Place a Layer Stack Legend and an Impedance table in the fabrication drawing so the fabricator sees the required construction and tolerances.

tools.name: Composite Drill Drawing and Final Artwork
tools.description: Composite outputs that overlay several layers into a single plot for documentation: Composite Drill Drawing shows the outline plus drill symbols, and Final Artwork Prints produce a per-layer or composite view suitable for a drawing package rather than for photoplotting.
tools.usage: Fabrication Outputs > Composite Drill Drawing / Final Artwork Prints; or as outputs in an OutJob
tools.example: Add a Composite Drill Drawing output wired to the documentation PDF container.

tools.name: Pick and Place file
tools.description: The component centroid data used by the placement machine: designator, comment/value, footprint, X and Y position, rotation and layer (side), in CSV or text form with a selectable unit and coordinate origin. It is generated per assembly variant so a variant's not-fitted parts are excluded.
tools.usage: File > Assembly Outputs > Generates pick and place files…; or add a 'Generates pick and place files' output in an OutJob

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Text or CSV.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: Imperial or metric.

parameters.name: Include components on
parameters.description: Top layer, bottom layer or both.

tools.example: Assembly Outputs > Generates pick and place files > CSV, metric, both sides > Generate; check that the origin matches the fiducial reference.
tools.notes: Rotation conventions differ between assemblers; confirm whether 0° means pin 1 top-left and supply a first-article check if unsure.

tools.name: Assembly drawings
tools.description: Per-side drawings showing component outlines, designators and the board outline for the assembler. They are produced either as Assembly Outputs (Assembly Drawings) using the assembly mechanical layers, or — better — as a Draftsman Board Assembly View that also carries BOM tables, notes and detail views and updates with the board.
tools.usage: File > Assembly Outputs > Assembly Drawings…; or Draftsman: Place > Board Assembly View
tools.example: Draftsman document > Place > Board Assembly View (Top) > Place > BOM Table > Place > Note; include the Draftsman document as a Documentation output.

tools.name: Draftsman output
tools.description: Adds a Draftsman document to an OutJob so its live fabrication or assembly drawing is rendered to PDF or print with the rest of the release. Because Draftsman views are linked to the board, the released drawing always matches the released Gerbers.
tools.usage: OutJob > Documentation Outputs > Draftsman > select the .PcbDwf document; wire it to a PDF container
tools.example: Wire 'Draftsman - fabrication.PcbDwf' to the Documentation PDF container and regenerate after every board change.

tools.name: Bill of Materials (Report Manager)
tools.description: Generates a BOM from the project's components and parameters. The Report Manager dialog chooses the columns, the grouping and sorting, the supplier columns, the variant, and the output format — Excel (with a template), CSV, text, XML, HTML or PDF. For supply-chain-aware BOMs, ActiveBOM is the better source.
tools.usage: Reports > Bill of Materials…; or add a 'Bill of Materials' report output in an OutJob

parameters.name: Grouped Columns
parameters.description: Which parameters collapse identical parts into one line (typically Comment and Footprint).

parameters.name: Template
parameters.description: An Excel .XLT template giving the company BOM layout.

parameters.name: Export Options
parameters.description: File format, whether to open after export, and whether to add the file to the project.

parameters.name: Include parameters from
parameters.description: Database, part choices and supplier data columns.

tools.example: Reports > Bill of Materials > group by Comment and Footprint > add MPN and Manufacturer columns > template company_bom.XLT > Export.
tools.notes: Variants produce separate BOMs; set the variant in the output's properties so each SKU gets a correct list.

tools.name: ActiveBOM output
tools.description: Renders the project's .BomDoc — with its resolved part choices, supplier data, lifecycle flags and per-variant lines — to Excel, CSV, PDF or XML through an OutJob. Because the part choices live in the BomDoc rather than in the output template, the released BOM carries approved, purchasable part numbers.
tools.usage: OutJob > Report Outputs > Bill of Materials > select the BomDoc as the data source
tools.example: Wire the ActiveBOM output to the release container and export as both Excel (for purchasing) and CSV (for the assembler).

tools.name: Component Cross Reference Report
tools.description: Lists components grouped by library reference or by sheet, showing where each is used across the project. It complements the BOM for design reviews: it answers 'which sheets use this part?' rather than 'how many do we buy?'.
tools.usage: Reports > Component Cross Reference…; or add a Component Cross Reference Report output in an OutJob
tools.example: Reports > Component Cross Reference > group by Library Reference > export to Excel.

tools.name: Simple BOM and Report Project Hierarchy outputs
tools.description: Lightweight report outputs available in an OutJob: Simple BOM produces a plain text/CSV parts list without the Report Manager's configuration, and Report Project Hierarchy writes the compiled sheet structure. Both are useful as machine-readable artefacts inside a release package.
tools.usage: OutJob > Report Outputs > Simple BOM / Report Project Hierarchy
tools.example: Add both to the release OutJob so every release ships a plain parts list and a hierarchy record.

tools.name: Netlist outputs
tools.description: Exports connectivity in a foreign format as part of a release: Protel, PADS, EDIF, Verilog, VHDL, SPICE, Telesis and others, generated for the project or a single document. Within Altium these are only needed for interoperability, not for the schematic-to-PCB flow.
tools.usage: OutJob > Netlist Outputs > <format>; or Design > Netlist for Project > <format>
tools.example: Add a Protel netlist output for the customer's incoming inspection system.

tools.name: PDF documentation output (Smart PDF)
tools.description: Publishes schematics, PCB prints, BOM and Draftsman documents into a single bookmarked PDF with optional net and component hyperlinks, so a reviewer can click a net name and jump to where it is used. Available both as the Smart PDF wizard and as documentation outputs wired to a PDF container in an OutJob.
tools.usage: File > Smart PDF…; or OutJob > Documentation Outputs > Schematic Prints / PCB Prints / PCB 3D Prints wired to a PDF container

parameters.name: Export scope
parameters.description: Whole project or the current document.

parameters.name: Include component parameters / nets
parameters.description: Generates a parameter table and net hyperlinks in the PDF.

parameters.name: Additional bookmarks
parameters.description: Per-net, per-component and per-pin bookmarks for navigation.

parameters.name: Zoom / Colour
parameters.description: How much of the sheet a hyperlink zooms to, and mono/colour/grey output.

tools.example: File > Smart PDF > whole project > include the schematics and a 3D PCB print > generate nets and component bookmarks > review.pdf.

tools.name: Schematic Prints / PCB Prints
tools.description: The print outputs themselves. Schematic Prints selects which sheets and how they are scaled; PCB Prints builds printouts from named layer combinations (the 'Printout' configuration) so, for example, one printout shows Top copper plus pads and outline, another shows the silkscreen. Each printout is a page in the container.
tools.usage: OutJob > Documentation Outputs > Schematic Prints / PCB Prints; right-click > Configure to edit printouts and layer sets
tools.example: PCB Prints > Configure > create printouts 'Top Copper', 'Bottom Copper', 'Top Overlay', 'Drill Drawing' > wire to the PDF container.

tools.name: PCB 3D Prints / PDF3D
tools.description: Renders the board in 3D into the documentation set: a static 3D view as an image, or a PDF3D output that embeds an interactive, rotatable 3D model in the PDF so a reviewer without Altium can inspect the assembly. Views and camera positions are saved as named 3D configurations.
tools.usage: OutJob > Documentation Outputs > PCB 3D Print / PCB 3D Video; File > Export > PDF3D…
tools.example: File > Export > PDF3D > include all 3D bodies > board3d.pdf; the mechanical engineer rotates the assembly in Acrobat.

tools.name: Validation outputs
tools.description: Outputs that run checks rather than produce artwork: Design Rule Check (batch DRC and its report), Electrical Rules Check / project validation, Differences Report between two documents or revisions, and Footprint Comparison Report between the design and the libraries. Including them in the release OutJob makes checking part of the release rather than a habit.
tools.usage: OutJob > Validation Outputs > Design Rule Check / Electrical Rules Check / Differences Report / Footprint Comparison Report
tools.example: Add Design Rule Check and Footprint Comparison Report to the release OutJob; the Project Releaser then blocks on unresolved errors.

tools.name: Footprint Comparison Report
tools.description: Compares every footprint used on the board against the current version in the source library and reports any that differ, so a board that was laid out with an older or locally modified footprint is caught before release. It is the library-integrity check that complements the DRC's geometric checks.
tools.usage: OutJob > Validation Outputs > Footprint Comparison Report; or Reports > … in the PCB editor
tools.example: Run the report before release; investigate every 'differs from library' entry and either update the board or the library.

tools.name: Export > DXF/DWG
tools.description: Writes selected PCB layers as AutoCAD DXF or DWG for mechanical documentation or for a fabricator that wants the profile in 2D CAD. Options select which layers map to which DXF layers, the units, the scale and the DXF/DWG version. The reverse import brings a mechanical outline in onto a chosen layer.
tools.usage: File > Export > DXF/DWG…; File > Import > DXF/DWG…
tools.example: File > Export > DXF/DWG > format AutoCAD 2013, units mm, export Mechanical 1 and Top Overlay > outline.dxf.

tools.name: Export > IDF / IDX
tools.description: The classic ECAD-MCAD interchange: IDF exports the board outline, cutouts, keepouts and component placements with heights as a .emn/.emp pair that most mechanical CAD packages import; IDX is the incremental, change-based successor used for round-trip collaboration where each change set is reviewed and accepted.
tools.usage: File > Export > IDF…; File > Export > IDX (and File > Import > IDX for the return path)
tools.example: File > Export > IDF > board.emn + board.emp, and hand them to the mechanical engineer for the enclosure model.
tools.notes: MCAD CoDesigner is the modern replacement for IDF/IDX round-tripping; use IDF only where the MCAD tool has no CoDesigner plug-in.

tools.name: Export > Hyperlynx and Ansys EDB
tools.description: Exports the board to dedicated signal- and power-integrity solvers: Siemens Hyperlynx (.hyp) and the Ansys Electronics Database used by SIwave and HFSS. These carry the stackup, materials and geometry so a full-wave or transmission-line analysis can be run outside Altium's built-in screening SI tool.
tools.usage: File > Export > Hyperlynx…; File > Export > Ansys EDB… (availability depends on the installed exporter extensions)
tools.example: File > Export > Hyperlynx > board.hyp, then run the post-layout simulation of the DDR bus in Hyperlynx.
tools.notes: Both exporters are delivered as extensions; if the menu item is missing, install it from Extensions and Updates.

tools.name: Export > PADS / Specctra / other EDA formats
tools.description: Outbound translators to other EDA systems: PADS Layout ASCII, Specctra design (.dsn) and session (.ses) for external autorouters, P-CAD ASCII and others depending on the installed exporter extensions. The Specctra route is the classic way to use a third-party autorouter and bring the result back.
tools.usage: File > Export > PADS Layout / Specctra Design…; File > Import > Specctra Session
tools.example: File > Export > Specctra Design > route externally > File > Import > Specctra Session to bring the routing back.

tools.name: CAM Editor
tools.description: Altium's viewer and editor for manufacturing data. It opens generated Gerber, ODB++ and NC drill files, lets layers be aligned, netlists extracted and compared against the PCB, and provides measurement and DFM inspection — the independent check that the released data really is the board.
tools.usage: File > Open… on the generated Gerber/drill files (the CAM Editor opens them); Tools within the CAM document for netlist extraction and comparison
tools.example: Open the generated .gbr set in the CAM Editor, extract the netlist, and compare it with the PCB's netlist to confirm nothing was lost in output generation.
tools.notes: Delivered as an extension; install 'CAM Editor' from Extensions and Updates if the files open as plain text.

tools.name: Post Processing outputs (copy/zip/command)
tools.description: OutJob outputs that act on the results: copy files, create a zip archive of a container's contents, or run an external command. They make a release self-packaging — for example zipping the fabrication folder with a date-stamped name ready to send to the fabricator.
tools.usage: OutJob > Post Processing > Copy Files / Zip Files / Run Command
tools.example: Add a Zip Files post-processing output over the Fabrication container producing `[Project Name]_fab_[Date].zip`.

tools.name: Print (direct)
tools.description: Sends the active schematic or PCB straight to a printer or PDF writer with page setup, scale, colour mode and, for the PCB, the printout/layer configuration. It is the quick path for a single sheet; a full document set should go through an OutJob so it is repeatable.
tools.usage: File > Print… (Ctrl+P); File > Page Setup…; PCB: File > Print Preview then Configure for layer printouts
tools.example: File > Page Setup > Scale Mode: Fit Document On Page, Colour Set: Mono > Print Preview > Print.

tools.name: Generated files folder and output paths
tools.description: By default Altium writes outputs under the project folder in Project Outputs / Project Logs directories, with the exact path controlled per output container and by Project Options > Options (Output Path, 'Use separate folder for each output type'). Getting this structure right is what makes a release package navigable and repeatable.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options > Options tab > Output Path and Output Options; container path tokens such as [Project Name], [Output Type], [Date]
tools.example: Set the container path to `Outputs\[Output Type]` with 'Use relative path' so the release folder structure is identical on every machine.

tools.name: Release the project (manufacturing package)
tools.description: Running the configured OutJobs through the Project Releaser produces an immutable, revisioned manufacturing package in the Workspace rather than a folder on someone's disk. The package links the generated data back to the exact source snapshot, so any released board can be reproduced years later.
tools.usage: Project > Project Releaser… (requires a connected Workspace and OutJobs marked for release)
tools.example: Mark the Fabrication and Assembly OutJobs as release-managed, run Project > Project Releaser, review the generated data, and Release.
tools.notes: The releaser runs the validation outputs first; a design with DRC errors will not release unless they are explicitly accepted.
